idea: Annual AI adoption benchmark report for UK asset managers
buyer: COOs and heads of research at asset managers
pain: Nobody knows if their AI rollout is ahead or behind peers
v1: Survey 30 firms, publish a paid 40-page benchmark
channel: Her AI-adoption reputation plus fund network
verdict: Rare combination: high fit, recurring, defensible via accumulating data, and the buyer has budget.

why.distribution: 20-50 warm firms via her own network and the AI-adoption remit that made her visible.
why.demand: Firms buy benchmark reports routinely, but nothing tested here yet.
why.fmf: She led exactly this inside a firm - both the finance and the AI-change-management halves.
why.revenue_structure: Annual licence that renews by habit once it becomes the reference point.
why.defensibility: The response dataset compounds; year three is impossible for a new entrant to replicate.
why.leverage: One report sells to every firm; survey admin is the only per-customer cost.
why.time_to_revenue: Needs a survey round before publication: 4-6 months.
why.tailwind: AI adoption spend in professional services is the strongest budgeted trend available to her.
why.ceiling: £4k x 40 licences = £160k; reaching 40 buyers in year one is optimistic.

ceiling_arithmetic: £4k x 40 firm licences = £160k. UK asset management has enough firms, but 40 paying in year one from a standing start is the stretch case; 15-20 is realistic = £60-80k. Year two with an established benchmark clears £200k.
carries: The only idea in the set where a compounding proprietary dataset sits under a high-fit, high-tailwind product.
kills: Nothing structural. Year one is a chicken-and-egg problem: the report needs respondents before it has buyers.
test: Ask ten heads of research whether they would answer a 20-minute survey AND pay £4k for the aggregate.
test_pass: Six agree to respond and two say they would buy.
test_fail: They will answer but not pay - which makes it marketing, not a business.
